drivingQuestion: What practical difference is there between Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya, if both bar dedicating all one's property?
outcomeNote: The difficulty of arakhin.28a.9 is answered: the two tannaim differ over whether the Usha cap of a fifth applies, and an incident is brought illustrating that cap.

segments.he: אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ דְּרַבִּי אִילָא, דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אִילָא: בְּאוּשָׁא הִתְקִינוּ, הַמְבַזְבֵּז אַל יְבַזְבֵּז יוֹתֵר מֵחוֹמֶשׁ.
segments.en: The Gemara responds: «There is» a practical difference «between them» with regard to the statement «of Rabbi Ila, as Rabbi Ila said: In Usha» the Sages «instituted» that «one who dispenses» his money to charity «should not dispense more than a fifth.» Rabbi Eliezer, who did not state that one should spare his property, rules that one may give all his money to charity, provided he keeps a small portion for himself, whereas Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya maintains that one should not give more than a fifth.

segments.he: מַעֲשֶׂה בְּאֶחָד שֶׁבִּקֵּשׁ לְבַזְבֵּז יוֹתֵר מֵחוֹמֶשׁ, וְלֹא הִנִּיחוּ לוֹ חֲבֵרָיו. וּמַנּוּ? רַבִּי יְשֵׁבָב, וְאָמְרִי לַהּ: רַבִּי יְשֵׁבָב, וְלֹא הִנִּיחוּ לוֹ חֲבֵירָיו. וּמַנּוּ? רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא.
segments.en: The Gemara relates that there was «an incident involving a certain» individual «who sought to dispense more than a fifth» of his property as charity, «and his friend did not let him» act upon his wishes. «And who» was this friend? It was «Rabbi Yeshevav. And some say» it was «Rabbi Yeshevav» who wanted to give too much charity, «and his friend did not let him» do so. «And who was» the friend? It was «Rabbi Akiva.»
